learning_outcomes.text: Analyze and design electronic circuits at high frequency and antennas, with an emphasis on integrated circuits for wireless communication transceiver and radar.

syllabus_topics: Power Amplifiers (class A, B, C, AB)
LTSPICE Laboratory Exercise: The design of passive filters and multistage MOSFET amplifier.
Transmit/receive antennas and their characteristic parameters.
Radio-Frequency Identification (RFID) systems: basic operation, applications in LF, HF, and UHF bands, tag and reader types.
Overview of key IoT technologies: Bluetooth, WiFi, ZigBee, Z-Wave, UWB.
Wireless power transfer and energy harvesting.
Radar: operating principles, Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave mode.
On-chip radar architectures for automotive applications.
Measurement of millimeter-wave radar-on-chip (120 GHz) for automotive applications, using MATLAB.
teaching_methods: Lab Exercises concerning numerical simulations of RF electronic circuits with the aid of a PC
Measurements for 120 GHz radar (silicon radar) in an automotive environment and comparison with MATLAB-based numerical codes
Laboratory measurements of antennas (dipoles and Yagi-Uda antennas) and comparison with antenna toolbox codes

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam on course topics, including tests on lab exercises

assessment_rules: To pass the exam, the student is required to demonstrate acquisition of fundamental concepts on analysis and design of main blocks of a RF transceiver system and related circuit components. Students may take the exam for both modules in a single session or in two separate sessions. The final grade will be calculated as the average of the grades earned on the individual modules.
